title: Future State — Fish Ready Prep
timeHorizon: Revisit in about one year after the pond has been established and observed through the seasons.
goal: Decide whether adding a small fish population is appropriate only after the pond has proven stable in Arizona conditions, then prepare the system without changing the established visual design.
currentDecision: No pothos. Keep the finished pond look as currently designed. Fish are not part of the initial build.
brainstormingTopics: Review real summer water temperatures and how much daily temperature swing the pond experiences.
Confirm dissolved-oxygen/aeration needs during the hottest weather.
Verify the Phase 3 mechanical and biological filtration has matured and has enough capacity for a small fish load.
Reassess whether the approximately 50-gallon-class pond is suitable for fish at all in the final location and heat exposure.
Choose only small fish species and a conservative stocking level appropriate for the actual water volume and Arizona heat; no koi.
Decide whether dedicated aeration should be added before fish.
Plan water testing, acclimation and a heat/emergency response before introducing fish.
Keep the existing lotus, Buddha, fountain and jasmine appearance unchanged unless a fish-safety need requires a minor functional change.

shoppingList.note: No purchases or budget are committed for this future idea. Estimate and shopping items will be created only if the fish plan is activated in roughly a year.
